legend.target_workload: the workload nominated before timing; its whole-model win must repeat before installation
legend.timing_case: the captured input case behind this hypothesis's local kernel timings
legend.timing_workload: the workload behind a region's recorded shipped-kernel speedup
legend.model_ratios: per-workload products of incremental model ratios; diagnostic estimates, not final measurements
legend.p: share of one step this region costs, all copies together, per workload
legend.T_orig_ms: library time for all copies, per workload, from pricing
legend.T_rep_ms: library time for one copy, per workload, from pricing
legend.roofline_ms: estimated ideal cost of one copy from boundary traffic and arithmetic
legend.s_max: optimistic headroom estimate: library time divided by estimated ideal cost
legend.bound: estimated limiting resource: memory, known compute, or launch; custom arithmetic may be unknown
legend.s: speedup shipped: the library's time over the shipped kernel's, both from the kernel's own ship clock
legend.region_ms: the kernel's time for one pass of one copy, from the ship clock
legend.library_ms: the library's time for the same pass, measured beside it
legend.win_ms: library_ms minus region_ms; positive means the kernel is faster
legend.sigma_ms: uncertainty of win_ms; a ship needs a win past three of these
legend.stranded: regions dropped before the search, grouped by reason
legend.steps_per_sample: dependent model steps in one timed sample of the step clock; more than one when a step is too short to bring the GPU clock up on its own
legend.min_win_ms: the least a region win had to save per step on this workload: 1% of the step, at most constants.min_win_ms; the three-sigma rule decides the rest
legend.speedup_vs_plain: under the compiled baseline: the finished model against plain eager MLX, paired in one window at the end of the job; compile's own gain is included, since the model runs compiled
legend.speedup_vs_compiled: under the plain baseline: the finished model (eager plus its kernels) against the untouched model under mx.compile, measured the same way; under 1 means compile alone is faster
legend.plain_win_confirmed: whether that comparison resolved a win past three sigma (compiled_win_confirmed likewise)
legend.plain_loss_confirmed: whether it resolved a loss (compiled_loss_confirmed likewise)
legend.measured_compute_gflops: the plain-matmul rate per dtype clocked in the region's own pricing window; the compute term of its estimated limit divides the region's flops by it
legend.close_rule: why a region's search ended: its budget or the job's is spent, the operator asked to finish, or no discernible headroom (launch-bound, head unmoved by the last two attempts, the last three kernels each within one sigma of the launch floor clocked beside them)
legend.constants.openers_per_region: how many attempts a region's widening round holds at most, each an opener written against the scaffold from a different agent-generated direction; limited by the remaining attempt budget
legend.delivery: how a kernel installs at the region's scope, per workload: direct, graph (the scope compiled with the cut inserted) or replay
legend.library_arm: what the region's clocks ran the library as, per workload: plain ops, or one compiled graph where graph delivery compiles the scope
legend.baseline.clocks_ms.compiled: under library inference: the model with its outermost compilable scopes compiled and empty, the baseline unless the manifest asks for plain
legend.final.delivery: under a plain baseline: the untouched model against the installed scopes compiled with no kernel, and that against the patched model

hypotheses.hypothesis: the harness's starting kernel
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: threadgroup-tiled matmul with 4x4 register blocking and fused multiply
hypotheses.hypothesis: one dispatch: each 8x8-thread threadgroup owns a 32x32 output tile, stages 32-wide K slabs of A (transposed) and B in threadgroup memory, every thread accumulates a 4x4 register block, and the epilogue multiplies by in2 before the single store, removing the tmp0 round trip and cutting global traffic by ~32x versus the scaffold's per-thread global streaming
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: use the hardware simdgroup matrix units: each simdgroup computes a 32x32 block as 4x4 simdgroup_float8x8 accumulators fed from threadgroup-staged A/B slabs via simdgroup_load, then stores to threadgroup memory and applies the in2 multiply on the way out; this trades ALU FMAs for the tensor path, which is the only route to the compute roofline here
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: row-strip kernel with float4 B reads and no threadgroup memory
hypotheses.hypothesis: each thread computes 1 row x 8 columns; B rows are read as two float4 vectors (contiguous along n) straight from global so the L1/L2 serve reuse across the 32 threads of a simd that share the same k, and A[row,k] is loaded once per k per thread; tests whether cache reuse alone beats explicit tiling at this small size where launch and barrier overheads matter
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: one output row per threadgroup with A row in shared memory
hypotheses.hypothesis: 256 threadgroups, one per output row, each 256 threads own one column; the A row is copied once into threadgroup memory and broadcast, B is streamed column-wise once per row with the k loop unrolled 8x; maximizes threadgroup count across the 10 cores so latency of the B column walk is hidden by occupancy rather than reuse
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: four rows per threadgroup with float4 shared A and 4 accumulators per thread
hypotheses.hypothesis: row_per_tg was best but each FMA needs one shared load and one global B load; staging 4 A rows transposed as float4 per k lets each thread compute 4 outputs with one float4 shared load and one B load per 4 FMAs, keeping 64 threadgroups x 256 threads (16k threads, 6.4 tgs per core) which is far more occupancy than tile_reg4x4's 4096 threads; expect load-issue pressure to drop ~2x
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: 16x16 tiles with 2x2 register blocking and 256 threadgroups
hypotheses.hypothesis: tile_reg4x4 had good load/FMA ratio but only 64 threadgroups of 64 threads; shrinking the tile to 16x16 with 8x8 threads each computing 2x2 yields 256 threadgroups so every core holds ~25, trading some reuse for occupancy
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: 4 rows x 2 columns per thread with float2 B reads
hypotheses.hypothesis: extend rows4_f4shared: each thread owns two adjacent columns read as one float2 from B, computing 8 outputs per k with one float4 shared load and one float2 global load; halves global load instructions again at the cost of 128 threads per threadgroup
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: eight rows per threadgroup with 512 threads splitting K in halves and a shared reduction
hypotheses.hypothesis: rows4_f4shared is the best; doubling reuse to 8 rows per B load halves global load instructions per FMA, and splitting K across two 256-thread halves keeps 512 threads per threadgroup (32 tgs x 512 = 16k threads, same occupancy as head) with a cheap 8-float shared reduction at the end; expects fewer B loads per output at unchanged occupancy
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: four rows per threadgroup with split-K over two halves for 32k threads
hypotheses.hypothesis: keep head's 4-row float4 layout but split K over two 256-thread halves per threadgroup so 64 tgs x 512 threads = 32k threads are in flight; tests whether more thread-level parallelism (halving per-thread latency chain) beats head
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.kind: two rows per threadgroup with float2 shared A
hypotheses.hypothesis: probe the occupancy/reuse tradeoff between row_per_tg (256 tgs, 1 out/thread) and rows4 (64 tgs, 4 out/thread) with 128 tgs of 256 threads computing 2 outputs each
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: the harness's starting kernel
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: 64 threadgroups of 128 threads; each threadgroup stages a 32x32 A and B panel in threadgroup memory per 32-wide K step, each of its 4 SIMD groups owns a 16x16 output block as four 8x8 simdgroup_float8x8 accumulators fed by simdgroup_load/multiply_accumulate. Uses the matrix units rather than scalar FMAs and cuts global traffic 32x versus the scaffold; differs from the register-blocking and streaming designs by using hardware mma with a K-staged shared tile.
hypotheses.summary: shipped: whole-model correctness and independent timing confirmation passed

hypotheses.hypothesis: 64 threadgroups of 256 threads; classic K-tiled shared-memory GEMM where each thread owns a 2x2 output block (16k threads in flight, matching the occupancy the prior region found decisive) with float4 cooperative loads of 32x32 A/B tiles. Tests whether a shared-memory tile with high thread count beats mma at this size; no simd matrices.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.hypothesis: 256 threadgroups x 256 threads, one output row per threadgroup: the A row is loaded once into threadgroup memory as float4, then each thread computes one column with B reads coalesced across the threadgroup and A read from shared with a k-unrolled loop of 4 independent accumulators to hide latency. Maximum thread count and no barriers inside the k loop; differs from both tiled designs by using no output blocking at all.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.kind: split-K across SIMD lanes with simd_sum
hypotheses.hypothesis: Each 32-lane SIMD group computes an 8-row x 8-column output block by splitting K across its 32 lanes (each lane handles K/32 with float4 loads), accumulating 64 partials per lane in registers and reducing with simd_sum. 4 simd groups per threadgroup, 1024 threadgroups worth of blocks give very high occupancy with in-register reuse; differs from others by parallelizing K instead of M/N within a group.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.kind: simdgroup loads straight from device memory
hypotheses.hypothesis: Keep the mma32 tiling (64 tgs x 4 SIMD groups, 16x16 per group) but drop the threadgroup staging: simdgroup_load reads A and B 8x8 fragments directly from device memory with the row stride, removing both barriers and the shared-memory write/read per K step. At 256^3 the tiles fit in L1 so the redundant device reads should be cheap while the barrier latency and staging instructions disappear.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.kind: register prefetch of next K panel
hypotheses.hypothesis: mma32 with software pipelining: load the next 32-wide A/B panel into registers before the mma loop of the current panel, store to shared afterwards, so global latency overlaps matrix compute; one barrier per step instead of two.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.hypothesis: 128 threadgroups of 128 threads, each covering a 16x64 output tile (4 SIMD groups side by side, 16x16 each) with a 64-wide K step: twice the threadgroups across 10 cores and half the barrier count; tests whether occupancy or barrier count limits mma32.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.kind: padded shared stride to avoid bank conflicts
hypotheses.hypothesis: mma32 tiling unchanged, but As/Bs rows are padded to a 36-float stride so the float4 stores and simdgroup_load fragment reads no longer hit the same banks every 32 floats; tests whether threadgroup-memory bank conflicts are the remaining cost over roofline.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: whole-model speedup unresolved

hypotheses.hypothesis: same 32x32 shared tile and 64 threadgroups, but only 2 SIMD groups each owning a 16x32 output block (8 accumulators): per kk step 2 A + 4 B fragment loads feed 8 mma instead of 4 loads per 4 mma, raising mma density per shared read and halving barrier participants.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.kind: double-buffered shared tile with one barrier
hypotheses.hypothesis: mma32 with two shared A/B buffers: store panel k+1 into the alternate buffer while mma consumes panel k, so only one barrier per K step is needed and no extra register prefetch is held; differs from mma_prefetch by staging directly rather than through registers.
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: slower than the installed kernel in a fresh region comparison; model timing skipped

hypotheses.hypothesis: 65536 threads each do one scalar multiply with no loop, maximizing threads in flight so the memory system sees the most outstanding requests; differs from vec4_flat by relying on occupancy rather than wide loads

hypotheses.kind: eight elements per thread two float4 loads
hypotheses.hypothesis: 8192 threads each issue two independent float4 loads per input before multiplying, giving each thread more memory-level parallelism with fewer threadgroups (32 of 256); tests whether per-thread ILP beats raw thread count at this tiny size
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: exactly 40 threadgroups of 256 threads (four per core) loop with a float4 grid stride over the whole array; fixes threadgroup count to a multiple of the core count so scheduling is even, trading fewer launches of groups for a small loop
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: scalar_flat was the best so far; this removes every inN_shape reference and the bounds check (a fallback_predicate guards the fixed 65536 size) so the harness binds no shape buffers, and uses 1024-thread groups (64 groups) to cut dispatch work per group; tests whether argument binding and per-group setup are the residual overhead behind the library

hypotheses.hypothesis: 32768 threads each move one float2 with no shape buffers or bounds check; between scalar (best) and float4 (worst) widths, tests whether an 8-byte access keeps enough threads in flight while halving instruction count
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: a 256x256 2-D grid with 32x8 threadgroups, index computed from x and y with no shape buffers; matches the library's likely 2-D contiguous dispatch and tests whether grid shape affects scheduling at this size
hypotheses.summary: correct_slower: region did not nominate an installable replacement

hypotheses.hypothesis: same shape-free scalar body but 64-thread groups (1024 groups) so many small groups spread across all 10 cores immediately; tests the opposite end of the group-size knob from scalar_noshape_tg1024

hypotheses.hypothesis: vec4_flat carried shape buffers and a bounds check; this repeats the float4 width with no shape buffers and a fallback predicate (like scalar_noshape_tg1024) so the only difference from the tied scalar/float2 kernels is 16-byte access. Tests whether the earlier float4 loss was the extra argument binding rather than the width.

hypotheses.kind: two strided scalar elements per thread
hypotheses.hypothesis: 32768 threads each load element i and i+32768 with two independent scalar loads before either multiply, keeping coalesced 4-byte accesses while halving threads and doubling in-flight loads per thread; differs from vec4_x8 by keeping scalar width and from float2 by using a stride instead of adjacency.
